$comment: A ratchet, not a style rule. There is no line count that is inherently wrong;
what is wrong is a module that concentrates change while quietly accumulating
ownership that belongs elsewhere. This file records where those modules stand
today so the number can go down and not up.
- a recorded module may not exceed its recorded line count;
- a module that drops more than `slack` lines below its record must have the
record lowered in the same change, so an improvement is banked rather than
left as headroom for the next regression;
- a production module that crosses `threshold` and is not recorded here fails
the build, so a new hotspot is a deliberate, reviewed entry rather than a
- every entry needs a `plan`, so an exception is a decision with an owner and
Generated files and *.test.ts are out of scope: tests are allowed to be long,
and a generator's output is owned by its generator.

packages/cli/src/commands/estate/estate..plan: Decomposing — see docs/architecture/estate-decomposition.md. Steps 0-1 done: -552 to estate-bundle-install.ts, -63 to estate-import-policy.ts, -214 to estate-contract-attestation.ts. Then -106 from routing every refusal through envelope.ts instead of building a JSON literal at each call site; that one is ownership, not just size — the envelope shape now has one owner. Remaining: the renderer, acquisition, the service, and runVerify. Its siblings estate-audit.ts and estate-adoption.ts are already pure domain with rendering split out; this is the un-migrated residue.

packages/cli/src/capability-composition..plan: Split graph construction / coordinate resolution / overlap analysis / policy / report projection. Composition stays audit-only. Queued behind estate.

packages/generators/src/deploy.ts.plan: Split provider-neutral deploy-plan validation from Cloud Run projection so a second target does not fork the file. Queued.

packages/cli/src/self-skill.ts.plan: Must stay derived from the command registry. Separate registry metadata from document projection; no manually maintained parallel command description.

packages/cli/src/commands/status.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 1554 for `--require`, which turns the verdict this module already computes into an exit code. status owns nextSafeAction, so the gate belongs here rather than in a new module; putting it elsewhere would have split the verdict from its consumer. Still queued: separate lane-freshness computation (domain) from the rendering, and share the certification-reading logic certify.ts duplicates.

packages/generators/src/certify.ts.plan: Holds a second certification model alongside @anvil/certification. See docs/architecture/certification-authority.md; do not grow it until that is resolved.

packages/cli/src/tool-cli.ts.plan: The shared generated-CLI engine. Separate argument decoding from execution and rendering. Queued.

packages/runtime/src/executor.ts.plan: Deliberately NOT queued for decomposition. execute() is a strictly ordered safety gauntlet; splitting it into stages trades a readable sequence for a reorderable pipeline. The control here is an ordering test, not a file split.

packages/cli/src/commands/estate/estate-.plan: Already pure domain with rendering separated — the shape estate.ts is being moved toward. Long, but not misowned; revisit only if it grows.

packages/compiler/src/classify.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 1116 for async-events Phase 1: classifyArchetype takes an isWebhookReceiver param (checked first, unconditionally — structurally certain from provenance), and findJobHandleField/findStateField are exported for reuse against webhook payloads. Cohesive: one inference pass over AIR. Watch for growth rather than split speculatively.

packages/compiler/src/protocols/postman..plan: One parser, one format. Splitting parsers by size would not improve ownership.

packages/air/src/schema.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 1081 for async-events Phase 0: AsyncContractSchema gained an optional webhook field and WebhookContractSchema/WebhookSignatureVerificationSchema (the Zod mirror of async-contract.ts's WebhookContract/WebhookSignatureVerification) were added alongside it, same file, same reason the two must stay structurally identical. The canonical model definition. Length is inherent to being the single source of truth; splitting it would scatter the authority.

packages/compiler/src/manifest.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 1077 for async-events Phase 1: a new async_contract manifest key (mirroring the existing idempotency key's pattern) lets a human hand-supply a complete AsyncContract.webhook — including its full signature_verification sub-block — for the common real-world case (Stripe, GitHub, Twilio, per the design doc's own vendor evidence) where no spec expresses this and the compiler must not guess it. Cohesive: manifest parsing plus enrichment application. Watch.

packages/compiler/src/gateway/receipt.ts.plan: Cohesive: receipt identity, digests, verification. Safety-adjacent; prefer tests over splitting.

packages/compiler/src/gateway/wso2/adapt.plan: One vendor adapter. Per-vendor files are the intended boundary.

packages/runtime/src/idempotency.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 979 for async-events Phase 2, Decision A: the job-handle index (LedgerEntry.jobId, complete()'s new optional secondaryKey param, findBySecondaryKey) needed in both InMemoryLedger and FirestoreLedger, the latter backed by its own sibling Firestore collection with the same create/verify/reconcile rigor the rest of the class already applies. Safety-critical. Prefer tests over splitting, as with executor.ts. Previously raised from 977 for a comment explaining why InMemoryLedger.durable is annotated `boolean` rather than inferred as the literal `false` — the class implements an interface that permits either, and the literal type prevented a durable test double from subclassing it.

packages/refinement/src/detect.ts.plan: Deterministic deficiency detection over AIR; cohesive. Watch.

packages/certification/src/checks.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 892 for async-events Phase 4: three new static checks (async_completion_source_present, webhook_signature_refs_resolve, webhook_remote_verify_host_allowed) plus the new CertificationDeployTarget seam they resolve refs against. Previously raised from 884 for Phase 0's optional-statusOperationId guards. Expected to grow if certification truth consolidates here; raise deliberately with that change, not incidentally.

packages/generators/src/skill.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 883 for async-events Phase 0: asyncSurfaces() now skips a webhook-only resolution (no statusOperation to name a CLI command/tool for) rather than reporting nothing changed; its own long-running skill section lands with Phase 6. Watch.

packages/compiler/src/normalize.ts.plan: Raised deliberately from 814 for async-events Phase 1: merges webhookPathItems(doc) into the paths loop and adds attachWebhookLinks, which records a callbacks:-derived webhooks: link as an evidence claim rather than writing AsyncContract.webhook directly (see manifest.ts's async_contract key for why). Watch.
